brow: Aggregated snapshot · open-source compilation · not official reporting
editionNote: Morning edition. It covers the 24 hours to 05:10 CEST on 24 October; new research covers 17:10 CEST on 23 October to 05:10 CEST on 24 October, items from the previous edition still inside the 24 hours were carried, and stories with new developments are marked as follow-ups.

theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: Zelensky Says Starlink Caps Still Hobble Ukraine, Citing a Rubio Review Pledge
items.lede: The US Secretary of State told him by phone he would look again within three days, and Kyiv's own tests found the limits unchanged around the clock.

sections.text: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky told the Hudson Institute in Washington by video on 23 October that Starlink speeds in Ukraine were still capped at what he described as a limit of 161 kilometres per hour, or 100 miles per hour [1]. He said Secretary of State Marco Rubio had promised to revisit the issue within 48 to 72 hours, and that Ukrainian tests at night, morning, and daytime showed the limits still in place [1]. He proposed that, short of a full ceasefire, talks start with an energy truce, a ceasefire at sea, and prisoner exchanges [1]. No SpaceX or State Department statement was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that Zelensky said this, because a Ukrinform correspondent attended. Confidence on the US review is low, because only his account of the Rubio call was found.

items.title: Russian Strikes on Southern Odesa Region Injure Three and Set a Resort Ablaze
items.lede: Emergency crews said a repeat strike hit the fire site while they worked, and a company's warehouse and an office roof were partly destroyed elsewhere.

sections.text: Russian forces attacked the south of Ukraine's Odesa region on 23 October, injuring three people and damaging civilian, recreational, and industrial sites, Governor Oleh Kiper said [2]. The State Emergency Service said a large fire broke out at a recreation facility and that Russia struck the site again while rescuers were working, though none of them was hurt [2]. At another location an administrative building's roof and a company's production and warehouse premises were partly destroyed [2]. Fifty rescuers took part [2]. No Russian statement on the targets was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the injuries and damage, because the governor and emergency service are on record. Confidence is moderate overall, because no second outlet was found.

items.title: Drone Raid Shuts All Four Moscow Airports as Ukraine Hits an Oryol Plant
items.lede: Mayor Sobyanin reported 17 drones downed near the Russian capital, and hundreds of flights were cancelled or delayed before the all-clear at about 17:00 Moscow time.

sections.text: Russia's aviation agency Rosaviatsia closed Sheremetyevo, Domodedovo, Vnukovo, and Zhukovsky airports to arrivals and departures on the afternoon of 23 October during a drone raid on the capital, and Sheremetyevo sent passengers to shelters [3][4]. Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 17 drones were shot down on the approaches to Moscow [3][4]. FlightRadar24 counted 85 cancelled and 229 delayed flights at Sheremetyevo, and the all-clear came at about 17:00 Moscow time, TASS said [3]. The same day Oryol's governor confirmed a strike on an enterprise, which ASTRA identified as the Proton plant that makes electronic parts for Iskander-M missiles and Pantsir air defences [3]. Ukraine had not commented by the time of publication [3].

Confidence is high on the airport closures, because Russian officials are on record and two outlets agree. Confidence on the Oryol target is moderate, because it rests on ASTRA's open-source analysis.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine Both Set a 27 October Start for the Oleshky Truce
items.lede: Moscow and Kyiv fixed the pause for the early hours of 27 October, two days before the date in the White House release, to let aid in and civilians out.

sections.text: The White House said on 23 October that Russia and Ukraine had agreed, through First Lady Melania Trump, to halt all military action in Oleshky, in Russian-occupied southern Ukraine, from 29 October [5]. The pause is meant to let aid in and prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated passage [5][6]. The release put the remaining population at 1,700 to 2,000, mostly elderly, with about 50 children, against about 24,000 before the war [5]. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed the deal, said the two defence ministries were coordinating the timing, and said everyone wishing to leave could do so [7][8]. He said the evacuation would take at least several days [8]. Ukrainian faction leader Davyd Arakhamia thanked the Pope and the First Lady [9]. Ukraine's General Staff later set its own ceasefire in a designated area from 03:00 Kyiv time on 27 October [10]. Russian chief of staff Valery Gerasimov set the same moment, 04:00 Moscow time, for Russian troops, Reuters reported [11].

Confidence is high that all three governments back the truce and on the 27 October start, because White House, Kremlin, and Ukrainian General Staff statements were read and Moscow and Kyiv set the same time; the White House release gave 29 October.

items.title: Kremlin Sets Three-Way Talks With Ukraine and the US for Abu Dhabi in November
items.lede: Russia's spokesman Peskov named the first half of November, while Putin insisted the goal is a final deal rather than a short pause in fighting.

sections.text: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on 23 October that the next round of talks between Russia, Ukraine, and the US was planned for the first half of November in Abu Dhabi, in a trilateral format [12]. It would be the first such round since talks lapsed earlier this year [12]. Later on 23 October Zelensky said negotiators from Ukraine, Russia, and the US had agreed to technical-level meetings in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November; a US official said the next talks could be in Abu Dhabi or Switzerland [11]. In a state television interview aired late on 22 October, President Vladimir Putin said the talks must aim at security for Ukraine and Russia under a final agreement, not a short truce [13][14]. Zelensky told CNN he was ready for a ceasefire but needed strong security guarantees [14].

Confidence is high on Peskov's and Putin's statements, because AFP, Reuters, and CNBC carry them. Confidence on the date and venue is moderate: Zelensky confirmed Abu Dhabi and the first half of November, but a US official said Switzerland was also possible.

items.title: Strike on a Chernihiv Enterprise Kills One and Injures 25 in Northern Ukraine
items.lede: Eight victims were taken to hospital and people were briefly trapped under rubble, the city's military chief said, after Russia also hit a delivery depot.

sections.text: A Russian strike on an enterprise in Chernihiv, Ukraine, on 23 October killed one person and injured 25, city military administration head Dmytro Bryzhynskyi said [15]. He said 16 people were treated at the scene and eight taken to hospital, and that two enterprises had been hit, with people initially trapped under rubble [15]. He also reported an attack on a Nova Poshta delivery terminal in the north of the city [15]. No Russian statement on the target was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the toll, because the city head gave it on record. Confidence on the target is low, because the enterprise was not named and no second outlet was found.

items.title: Mariupol Defenders Among 270 Ukrainians Freed in a Swap With Russia
items.lede: Five survivors of the 2022 Olenivka prison blast came home in the first exchange in two months, and Moscow said its 270 returnees were waiting in Belarus.

sections.text: Ukraine and Russia each freed 270 people on 23 October, the first exchange in two months, President Zelensky said; Ukraine's 270 were 261 service members and nine civilians [16]. Most of the Ukrainians returning had been captured in the siege of Mariupol in spring 2022, including Azov fighters, border guards, and troops from the Ground Forces, Navy, and Air Assault Forces, and five survived the July 2022 Olenivka prison blast [16]. Ukraine's prisoner coordination headquarters said many had been convicted on sham charges in Russian captivity, and that nine of the returnees were civilians [16]. Russia's Defence Ministry said its freed soldiers were in Belarus and would be transported to Russia after medical and psychological care [12]. It was the 11th reported exchange of 2026 [16].
Confidence is high on the numbers, because Kyiv and Moscow give the same figure and two outlets report it.

items.title: Russia Hits Ukraine's Power Grid in Eight Regions, Cutting Supply to Over 500,000
items.lede: One DTEK thermal plant stopped generating and eight civilians died nationwide over the past day, as 176 drones flew at the country overnight.

sections.text: Russia launched 176 long-range drones, 92 of them jet-powered, at Ukraine overnight into 23 October, and air defences downed 140, with impacts at 19 locations, Ukraine's Air Force said [17][18]. Grid operator Ukrenergo reported power cuts in Zhytomyr, Donetsk, Khmelnytskyi, Volyn, Kharkiv, Poltava, Rivne, and Mykolaiv regions, and the Energy Ministry put those left without power above 500,000 [18][14]. DTEK said one of its thermal plants stopped generating after the attack, without naming it [18][14]. In Volyn alone almost 105,000 customers lost power and one person was hurt [19]. A daytime drone strike on an energy site in Lviv region later cut power to 175 settlements [20]. Regional authorities counted eight civilians killed and 67 wounded across the country over the past day [18].

Confidence is high on the drone count and the outages, because the Air Force, Ukrenergo, and DTEK are on record and two outlets agree. Confidence on the national casualty total is moderate, because it is a tally of regional reports.

items.title: Drones Set Russia's Azot Chemical Plant in Perm Region on Fire, Media Say
items.lede: Russia's Defence Ministry claimed 443 drones downed overnight, including over Perm, while the nitric acid made there supplies the country's explosives factories.

sections.text: Drones struck the Azot chemical plant in Berezniki, Perm region, Russia, on the morning of 23 October, and the plant was on fire, the Telegram channel ASTRA said in an OSINT analysis relayed by Ukrinform [21]. Russia's Defence Ministry said it destroyed 443 Ukrainian drones overnight and mentioned air defence activity over Perm region, without reporting damage [21][14]. The Uralchem plant makes ammonia, nitric acid, and ammonium nitrate, and nitric acid feeds Russian explosives and powder plants, Ukrinform said [21]. ASTRA reported an earlier attack on the site on 11 September [21]. No Ukrainian military claim was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate on the strike and fire, because they rest on one OSINT channel relayed by Ukrinform. Confidence is high on the 443-drone figure, because CNBC also reports it.

theaters.heading: Sabotage, drones, cyber, disinformation, and espionage targeting European states

items.title: Zelensky Warns Russia Will Use Drones and Sea Blockades to Pressure Europe
items.lede: Moscow aims to scare European voters into cutting aid, he said, while also claiming Russia plans to call up another 300,000 troops.

sections.text: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky told the Hudson Institute in Washington on 23 October that Russia had already sent drones against Romania, Germany, Poland, Moldova, and Bulgaria, and that day sank a grain ship off Romania [1]. He said Moscow would use drones as a tool of hybrid pressure, try to block the Black Sea to grain and energy shipping, and threaten cyber attacks to split the EU and erode support for Ukraine [1]. He also said Russia planned to mobilise another 300,000 troops, without giving a source [1]. No Kremlin reply was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that Zelensky said this, because a Ukrinform correspondent attended. Confidence on the mobilisation figure is low, because he offered no evidence and Ukraine is a party to the war.

items.title: Moldova Expels a Russian Diplomat After a Geran Drone Lands Near Homes
items.lede: President Sandu said Russia's war keeps putting her citizens at risk, after police found the drone about 100 metres from a house in Telenesti district.

sections.text: Moldova expelled a Russian diplomat on 23 October after a Russian Geran drone came down near family homes and an energy facility, President Maia Sandu said, calling it Russia's latest dangerous act [2]. Police said a resident found the drone in Kistelnita village, Telenesti district, about 100 metres from a house [2]. Moldova's Defence Ministry said a drone entered its airspace at 13:59 local time (12:59 CEST) during a large Russian attack on Ukraine, crossing from Ukraine's Vinnytsia region toward Moldova's Russian-controlled Transnistria region before vanishing from radar [2]. Moldova also logged several Russian drone incursions on 16 October [2]. No Russian response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that the drone fell and Sandu spoke, because police and the Defence Ministry are on record. Confidence is moderate on the expulsion details, because only one outlet was read.

items.title: Polish Prosecutors Probe a $30,000 Offer to Torch a Drone Factory Supplying Ukraine
items.lede: A journalist posing as a Belarusian job seeker exposed the recruiter, whose Telegram account traced to a Russian phone number, and the domestic security agency now leads the case.

sections.text: Prosecutors in Gliwice, Poland, opened an investigation on 21 October into an October attempt, via the Telegram chat 'Biełsatuszczyna', to recruit someone to set fire to the Flytronic plant in Gliwice for 30,000 US dollars on behalf of a foreign intelligence service, and handed it to the Internal Security Agency (ABW) [3][4]. TVP's Vot Tak exposed the plot after a reporter posing as a Belarusian job seeker was first offered money to burn cars with Ukrainian plates, and traced the recruiter's account to a Russian number in Saratov region [4]. Flytronic, part of WB Group, makes FlyEye reconnaissance drones used by Ukraine [4]. A WB Group site in Skarżysko-Kamienna burned in late August, which Prime Minister Donald Tusk called sabotage [4]. No Russian response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that the investigation exists, because the prosecutor's release was read. Confidence on Russian direction is moderate, because it rests on a journalist's tracing of a phone number.

items.title: Romania Blames Russia After a Drone Sinks a Cargo Ship Off Constanta
items.lede: One sailor died and three were missing, President Nicusor Dan said, in at least the seventh hit on merchant shipping near NATO's Black Sea coast in two weeks.

sections.text: A drone strike sank the Comoros-flagged cargo ship Khoryv about 13 nautical miles off Romania's port of Constanta, just outside Romanian territorial waters, on 23 October, Reuters reported [5]. Romania's naval authority said nine of the 13 Ukrainian and Azeri crew were rescued, one body was recovered, and three were missing [5][6]. President Nicusor Dan called it part of Russia's escalation in its war in Ukraine [5]. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned another Russian escalation in the Black Sea [7]. Reuters counts at least seven cargo ships hit off Romania and Bulgaria in two weeks, with some 30 sailors dead or missing, mostly near the Sulina Canal, Ukraine's main Danube export route [5]. No Russian response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the sinking and toll, because Romanian authorities and Reuters agree. Confidence on Russian responsibility is moderate, because it rests on Romania's attribution.

items.title: European Public Broadcasters Map About 100 Russia-Linked Hybrid Incidents
items.lede: The tally covers April to mid-October across 17 countries and excludes cyber operations, with the Black Sea the newest front, Belgium's RTBF said.

sections.text: Journalists in the Eurovision News Spotlight network documented about 100 incidents in 17 European countries between 1 April and 15 October 2026 that officials or media linked to Russia, Belgium's RTBF reported on 23 October [8]. The map covers physical attacks and recruited proxy agents and leaves out cyber attacks, influence operations, and espionage [8]. The latest cluster is in the Black Sea, where drones hit merchant ships off Romania and Bulgaria, with two deaths confirmed and at least ten missing since early October [8].
Confidence is moderate on the count, because it rests on attributions by officials and media that the project compiled rather than on court findings.

items.title: Ukraine's Military Intelligence Warns of Russian False-Flag Sabotage in the EU
items.lede: Kaliningrad, Russian Orthodox Church sites, and areas with Russian-speaking communities were among the possible targets listed, though the agency named no specific plots.

sections.text: Ukraine's Defence Intelligence (HUR) said on 23 October that Russia is preparing false-flag operations in Central and Eastern Europe, including the Baltic states, to blame on Ukraine [9][10]. HUR named two aims: discrediting Ukraine's forces to cut foreign support and intimidating European governments and societies [10]. Listed possible targets were critical infrastructure and border areas, the Kaliningrad exclave, areas with Russian-speaking populations, Russian Orthodox Church properties, and sites tied to Russian history [10]. HUR did not name specific planned attacks [10]. Russia denies involvement in sabotage in Europe [10].
Confidence is high that HUR made the warning, because two outlets carry it. Confidence on the alleged plans is low, because HUR is a party to the war and named no specific plots.

theaters.heading: Politics, security, and defense across the EU and NATO's European members

items.title: Italy Sends 500 Paratroopers to Milan as a New Security Decree Takes Effect
items.lede: Rome faces four separate protest initiatives on Saturday, the interior minister said, and a new movement will reveal its gathering points only at 14:30.

sections.text: Italy's new security decree, published in the official gazette on Friday, takes effect on Saturday and sends 500 soldiers to Milan after the 17 and 18 October clashes, Sky TG24 reported [1][2]. Undersecretary Alfredo Mantovano said on Rai 1 on Friday evening that the decree will be "fully operational" for Saturday's protests [1][2]. Interior Minister Matteo Piantedosi said attention extends beyond Milan to Rome, where four initiatives are planned [1]. Defence Minister Guido Crosetto complained the troops cannot use pepper spray or tasers, while Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini said they could deploy drones and Lince vehicles [1]. The new Movimento 17 ottobre said it would reveal three gathering points in each city only at 14:30, and the final square at 15:30 [1][2]. Police searched about 100 young people in 18 cities, 51 of them minors, after last weekend's unrest [1][2]. Milan mayor Giuseppe Sala said the city would not be militarised [1].
Confidence is high, because Sky TG24 and RaiNews report the deployment and protest plans, quoting ministers on record; turnout on Saturday is unknown.

items.title: Paris Police Ban the Agreed Bastille-to-Nation March, and French Unions Go to Court
items.lede: The prefecture's order allows only a 13:00 to 19:00 route along the city's outer boulevards, while a union march in Marseille was finally authorised.

sections.text: The Paris police prefecture in France banned on Friday afternoon the Bastille to Nation route it had agreed with unions a day earlier, and its order, published in the evening, allows the march only from Porte d'Italie to Porte de Vincennes from 13:00 to 19:00 [3][4]. The Ile-de-France union alliance refused the route, and CGT Paris co-general secretary Karl Ghazi told AFP it was "impossible to secure" [3]. The alliance will file an urgent challenge at the Paris administrative court on Saturday, franceinfo reported; the student federation Fage called the reversal "unacceptable" and said it raised the risk for marchers [5]. A union march in Marseille was finally authorised, while gatherings stay banned in Lyon [4]. In Bordeaux, the CGT, FSU, and FO filed a 14:00 route through the city centre [6]. The CGT called on 22 October for workplace meetings to generalise the 5 November strike [7]. No court ruling was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high, because the prefecture order and union positions are on record and reported by AFP, Europe 1, and franceinfo; the court challenge was announced but not yet filed by the cutoff.

items.title: Macron Meets Injured Officers as 70,000 French Police Brace for Saturday
items.lede: Prime Minister Lecornu said the threat from the ultra-left stays high, and his office asked Meta, Snap, and TikTok for special vigilance this weekend.

sections.text: French President Emmanuel Macron visited a police barracks in Paris's 19th district on Friday evening to thank security forces and meet officers injured in recent unrest, AFP reported [4]. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said 70,000 police and gendarmes will deploy on Saturday, including RAID, GIGN, and BRI elite units, about 20 Centaure armoured vehicles, and 15 water cannon, backed by Sentinelle soldiers [3][4]. He cited "many calls" from the ultra-left to commit violence and looting [3]. In Limoges, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said "the threat remains high" from the ultra-left and from criminals exploiting the unrest, and promised the state would rebuild the burned town hall identically [3]. Lecornu's office asked Meta, Snap, and TikTok for "particular vigilance" [4]. La France insoumise called the repeated restrictions an "authoritarian rush" [4]. The Paris SG against Lyon football match was moved to Monday at the prefecture's request [3]. No overnight incident report was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high, because the ministers spoke on record and AFP and Europe 1 report them; no remarks by Macron at the barracks were published by the cutoff.

items.title: Macron Calls the Trappes Drive-By Shooting a Racist Terrorist Attack
items.lede: A 26-year-old man of African origin died and a 12-year-old girl was hit eight times, and police also detained a close relative of the French suspect.

sections.text: French President Emmanuel Macron, visiting Trappes, west of Paris, France, on Friday evening, called the gun attack that killed one person and wounded five "a racist terrorist attack" and a "turning point" for the Republic [8][4]. The gunman fired from a grey Renault Clio for about 20 minutes, first in Trappes and then in La Verrière, and was blocked and arrested in Coignières at about 10:20, NOS reported, with AFP [9]. Police found a machine gun, tear-gas grenades, and gloves in his car [9]. The dead man was 26 and of African origin, and the 12-year-old girl was hit by eight bullets; three of the wounded are in a serious condition [9][8][10]. The National Anti-Terrorism Prosecutor's Office is investigating murder "in connection with a terrorist enterprise" [8][11], and a member of the suspect's immediate family was also taken into custody [8][9]. The 39-year-old suspect was known to police but not to the intelligence services [8]. No motive was announced by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the attack, the investigation, and Macron's words, because the prosecutor and president spoke on record and the BBC, NOS, and AFP report them; the victims' details rest on NOS and the mayor.

items.title: Brussels Shops Board Up Windows Before Saturday Protest Calls
items.lede: Belgian police say they will seek dialogue first, while the anonymous calls, some on AI-made flyers, name conflicting dates and stations.

sections.text: Brussels Mobility in Belgium said shared electric scooters and bikes will be barred from the Pentagon, the capital's historic centre, from 10:00 on Friday to 22:00 on Saturday [12][13]. The ban follows new calls for a city-centre protest on Saturday, after shared scooters were often wrecked and set on fire in earlier protests [13]. In Liège, hoteliers reported about 700 cancellations for the coming weekend, saying people do not feel safe because of the protests [13]. Shops on Brussels's Rue Neuve, including Nike, JD, and Hunkemöller, began boarding up their windows on Wednesday and workers were still at it on Friday morning, HLN reported, citing Belga [14]. Barricades also went up around Porte de Namur, Chaussée d'Ixelles, and Avenue Louise, and the operator Poppy barred ending trips in the centre from Friday 20:00 to Sunday morning [15]. Anonymous TikTok accounts, unlinked to unions or student groups, are circulating calls for Saturday, 31 October, or 2 November at Brussels-Central, Brussels-South, or Place Schuman, BRUZZ reported [16]. Police spokesman Christopher De Mesmaeker said police will "first seek contact" with young people to prevent confrontation [14]. No official protest request had been filed by the cutoff [15].
Confidence is high on the preparations, because Belga, BRUZZ, and 24Brussels report them and police spoke on record; turnout is unknown.

items.title: Marseille Drops Saturday Transit Halt as Nîmes Adds a Curfew for Minors
items.lede: France's curfew map keeps growing before the 24 October protests, with Paris nights restricted to Monday and Lyon publishing its exact protest-ban perimeter.

sections.text: The Paris police prefecture in France keeps its 23:00 to 06:00 curfew around Place de la République and Les Halles every night until Monday 26 October, for adults and minors [17][18][19]. On Friday the Bouches-du-Rhône prefect reversed his plan to suspend Marseille's public transport on Saturday, saying service will be run according to the public-order situation, while the adult curfew and the department-wide protest ban stay [20]. The Rhône prefecture published the order behind Saturday's Lyon protest ban, covering the Presqu'île, where more than 150 shops were damaged, the old town, the 6th district, and part of the 3rd [20]. The Gard prefect banned protests in parts of Nîmes and Alès and set a curfew for minors in central Nîmes from 22:00 Saturday to 05:00 Sunday [20]. Toulouse keeps a curfew in part of its centre until 05:00 Sunday [19]. Limoges will shut museums, a library, and sports sites on Saturday under prefecture orders [20].
Confidence is high, because the orders come from prefectures and are reported by CNews, franceinfo, and L'Internaute.

items.title: Britain Urges Households to Keep Three Days of Water and Food
items.lede: The UK advice covers storms and cyberattacks, El País said, and it arrived as Storm Austen cut power to thousands of homes in south-west England.

sections.text: The UK government's Be Ready campaign tells households to keep supplies for three days [21], including three litres of drinking water per person per day and food that needs no fridge or cooking [22]. El País reported on Friday that the government also advises spare phone batteries and a battery radio, following similar guidance in France, the Netherlands, and Ireland [22]. The paper said British intelligence has warned for weeks of sabotage and hybrid attacks by states such as Russia and Iran [22]. Storm Austen left thousands of homes in south-west England without power on Friday [22]. The campaign page was last updated on 21 October [21].
Confidence is high on the guidance, because the government page states it; the threat framing rests on El País.

items.title: France Jails 232 People and Opens 263 Organised-Gang Cases Over the Riots
items.lede: Justice Minister Darmanin said 1,144 people have been brought before prosecutors, and investigators have since arrested nearly 500 more suspects.

sections.text: French Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said on Friday that 232 people have been jailed over the looting and attacks on police of 17 and 18 October, up from 217 on Thursday [20][23]. He said 1,144 people have been referred to prosecutors, prosecutors have opened 263 cases on organised-gang charges, and more than 100 judicial investigations are under way [20]. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said nearly 500 people have been arrested through follow-up investigations since 17 October [20]. The Justice Ministry counts 2,700 people taken into custody since last Saturday, Al Jazeera reported, with AFP [24]. Darmanin said trials of those behind the worst violence will continue in the coming weeks [20].
Confidence is high, because the figures come from the two ministers on record, relayed by CNews and matched by Euronews and AFP; they are official counts not independently confirmed.

items.title: Italian Truckers Lift Most Southern Blockades Ahead of 27 October Talks
items.lede: Fuel stations in Campania still ran dry and a grocery chain head said Italy needs three to seven days to restock fresh food.

sections.text: Hauliers in Italy removed blockades in Campania, Calabria, Puglia, and Basilicata on Friday, and the last Naples pickets were cleared during the day, Corriere della Sera reported [25]. ANSA said deliveries to supermarkets resumed in Calabria as the protest waits for a 27 October meeting at the Transport Ministry [26]. Transport Minister Matteo Salvini said on 22 October that hauliers' leasing payments would be suspended until the end of March 2027, ANSA reported [27]. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called the remaining roadblocks 'intimidation' and said the government would use the law making road blocking a crime [27], and Justice Minister Carlo Nordio said mafia infiltration of the protests was 'highly probable' [28]. Many fuel stations in Campania were sold out, and the head of the Conad chain told ANSA a return to normal will take three to seven days, with fruit, vegetables, fish, and meat hit hardest [25]. Taxi unions plan a fuel-cost protest in Rome on 26 October [25]. The government put average self-service prices on Friday at 2.022 euros a litre for petrol and 2.260 for diesel [25].

Confidence is high, because Corriere della Sera and ANSA report the lifting and the ministers spoke on record; Nordio's view is his own assessment; the ANSA page was read only in part behind a consent wall.

items.title: Austria Expels Four Russian Diplomats Over Spying
items.lede: Three work at Moscow's embassy in Vienna and one at its OSCE delegation, and Russia's foreign ministry promised an unavoidable response.

sections.text: Austria's foreign ministry expelled four Russian diplomats for activities "incompatible with their diplomatic status", wording used for espionage, NOS reported [29]. Three work at the Russian embassy in Vienna and the fourth is a member of Russia's delegation to the OSCE, which is based in the city [29]. Russia's foreign ministry said a response would "inevitably" follow, NOS reported [29]. In May a former officer of Austria's domestic intelligence service was jailed for four years for spying for Russia [29]. No statement from the Austrian ministry itself was read by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because one major Dutch outlet reports the expulsions, citing the Austrian and Russian ministries.

theaters.heading: Security, politics, and Russian pressure on Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania

items.title: Lithuanian Border Guards Detain Six over Belarusian Balloon Cigarette Smuggling
items.lede: Officers have intercepted 181 balloon shipments from Belarus this year, against 635 in all of 2025, and forced down 67 smuggling drones.

sections.text: Lithuania's State Border Guard Service (VSAT) detained six people in Kėdainiai, central Lithuania, on Thursday, 22 October, on suspicion of smuggling cigarettes flown in from Belarus by balloon, Delfi reported via Elta on 23 October [1]. Officers watched four men unload boxes of Belarusian cigarettes at a private house, then stopped a second car whose two occupants allegedly escorted the shipment; all six are in custody, and the offence carries up to eight years in prison [1]. VSAT said it had intercepted 181 balloon shipments this year, 635 last year, and 226 in 2024, and had forced 67 smuggling drones to land this year [1]. 15min reported that two balloons landed in the Kėdainiai and Kaišiadorys districts after striking power lines, yet Vilnius and Kaunas airports kept flying, unlike earlier incidents [2].
Confidence is high on the detentions and counts, which Delfi attributes to VSAT; the airport detail rests on 15min's partly paywalled article.

items.title: Baltic Council Names Belarus a Growing Threat and Seeks EU Border Money
items.lede: Meeting in Tallinn, Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania called Russia the most significant long-term threat and asked the next EU budget to prioritise states bordering it.

sections.text: The 32nd Baltic Council, uniting the Baltic Assembly and the Baltic Council of Ministers of Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania, met in Tallinn on 23 October and adopted a joint statement [3]. It calls Russia the most significant, direct, and long-term threat to Euro-Atlantic security and says Belarus poses a growing challenge through military integration with Russia and the instrumentalisation of migration [3]. The three states pledged to keep developing the Baltic Defence Line, prioritise air and missile defence and counter-drone capabilities, and urged that EU defence funding, including Eastern Flank Watch, and the next Multiannual Financial Framework focus on countries bordering Russia and Belarus [3]. Estonian parliament speaker Lauri Hussar said the Baltic States must speak in one voice, finish Rail Baltica and Via Baltica, and answer Russian hybrid provocations [4].
Confidence is high on the statement's content, which comes from the published text, and on Hussar's remarks from the Riigikogu release.

items.title: Estonian Military Intelligence Says Putin Inflates Russia's Battlefield Gains in Ukraine
items.lede: Intelligence chief Ants Kiviselg put Russian losses at about 1,900 troops a day, with weekly losses above 10,000 for an eighth straight week.

sections.text: Ants Kiviselg, head of the Estonian Defense Forces Intelligence Center, told his weekly press conference that Russia's leadership consistently portrays the war in Ukraine more favourably than reality, citing Vladimir Putin's 16 October claim of 310 settlements and 6,500 square kilometres captured this year, ERR News reported [5]. He said an average of 240 combat engagements took place daily, heaviest on the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka axes in Donetsk Oblast [5]. Kiviselg said Russia's inaccurate portrayal of the line of contact could become a point of contention in any ceasefire talks, and that Moscow's efforts to shape perceptions of the front are cognitive warfare [5]. ERR said reports also emerged during the week of potentially hostile Russian satellite activity in space [5].
Confidence is high that Estonia's intelligence chief made these assessments, which ERR reports directly; the loss and engagement figures are Estonian estimates and were not independently checked.

items.title: Estonian Prosecutors Close Auvere Power Plant Drone Case Without Finding Origin
items.lede: Investigators even asked Ukrainian experts whether a stray Ukrainian drone hit the smokestack, but the wreckage was too badly destroyed to tell.

sections.text: Estonia's Prosecutor's Office has closed its criminal investigation into the drone that struck a smokestack at the Auvere Power Plant near the Russian border at 03:43 on 25 March, ERR News reported on 23 October [6]. State Prosecutor Gardi Anderson said the drone was so extensively destroyed in the collision and explosion that its origin could not be reliably determined, and that the case can be reopened if new evidence emerges [6]. The Internal Security Service (KAPO) said the information gathered did not indicate a deliberate act directed against Estonia, and Deputy Director General Andres Ratassepp warned that more such incidents should be expected while Russia's war against Ukraine continues [6]. The strike damaged the smokestack but injured no one and did not disrupt the power system [6].
Confidence is high on the closure and the officials' statements, because ERR quotes the prosecutor and KAPO directly; no prosecutor's office release was read.

items.title: Herem Expects Sharp Rise in Russian Threat Once Ukraine War Ends
items.lede: Estonia's new defence minister wants faster preparations, stronger air defences, and a public that understands the risks and how to respond.

sections.text: Estonian Defense Minister Martin Herem told ERR in an interview published on 23 October that the threat from Russia will increase dramatically from the moment it stops using its current resources in Ukraine [7]. He said he has set out that updated threat assessment at the Ministry of Defense, though he said it has not yet been formulated at government level or put on paper [7]. Herem said Estonia must accelerate defence preparations and strengthen air defences, adding that the country is not entering the drone warfare era completely barehanded [7]. The interview follows former ministry secretary general Kaimo Kuusk's claim that Herem cited a very different perception of the threat as the reason they could not keep working together; Herem said he would not describe anything as impossible [7].
Confidence is high on what Herem said, because ERR publishes the interview; the threat assessment itself is not public.

items.title: Lithuanian Companies Supply Metal Nets to Guard Strategic Sites from Drones
items.lede: The push follows the 18 October drone incursion, and one maker says its nets already cover some sites but would not name them.

sections.text: Lithuanian firms are producing anti-drone netting to protect the country's strategic objects, LRT reported on 23 October, citing the business daily Verslo Žinios [8]. Alvydas Pundzius of the company Kovas confirmed that its metal nets already protect some strategic objects but declined to give details [8]. Lithuania decided to increase anti-drone protection of strategic objects after the 18 October drone incursion, Verslo Žinios reported [8]. No Lithuanian government statement on the netting was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because LRT relays a single newspaper report and the company declined to give details.

items.title: Latvian Border Guards Find 13 Migrants in Smugglers' Car Far from Belarus
items.lede: Two Ukrainian drivers face people-smuggling charges, adding to 168 such criminal cases the State Border Guard has opened this year.

sections.text: Acting on a tip-off, Latvia's State Border Guard stopped a Volkswagen on a highway near Valmiera, in the north of the country, and found 13 people without valid documents who had illegally crossed the Belarusian-Latvian border, LSM reported on 23 October [9]. The driver and passenger, both Ukrainian citizens, face criminal proceedings for people smuggling and were themselves in Latvia without valid papers [9]. LSM noted that the location, far from the Belarus border, suggests the group may have been heading north towards Estonia or Finland rather than south towards Germany [9]. The State Border Guard has opened 168 criminal proceedings against 119 people this year for such offences [9].
Confidence is high on the stop and the case count, which LSM attributes to the State Border Guard; the route is LSM's inference.

items.title: Lithuania's Finance Minister Says Coalition Partners Pushed for Deep Defence Cuts
items.lede: Taurimas Valys says the government held defence spending above 5% of GDP despite a sizeable deficit and pressure to match the US minimum.

sections.text: Lithuanian Finance Minister Taurimas Valys told LRT.lt in an interview published on 23 October that there was considerable pressure, including from coalition partners, to sharply reduce defence spending while preparing next year's budget [10]. He said some proposed tying Lithuania to the minimum required by the United States, but the government 'stood firm' [10]. Valys said Lithuania's commitment to spend more than 5% of GDP on defence is already paying off, because investors no longer treat the country as a war zone [10]. He also faced opposition pressure, he said [10].
Confidence is high on Valys's remarks, because LRT publishes the interview; no coalition partner response was read.

theaters.heading: Stability, politics, and outside influence in the Western Balkans

items.title: Bosnia's UN Envoy Calls Republika Srpska Secession Threats Serious and Real
items.lede: Zlatko Lagumdžija expects the UN Security Council to renew the EUFOR Althea mission on 30 October despite Russian and Chinese positions.

sections.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina's UN ambassador Zlatko Lagumdžija told N1 that secession threats from Republika Srpska are serious and real and that its leadership has not stopped trying to weaken state institutions, Oslobođenje reported on 23 October [1]. He said Milorad Dodik is returning to earlier secessionist messages, but predicted that any attempt would be stopped [1]. Lagumdžija said a UN Security Council session on 30 October should decide on extending the EUFOR Althea mandate, which he expects to pass despite earlier blocking threats, and criticised Serbia's request to move the Hague tribunal archive to Belgrade [1]. The same day Dodik, marking 35 years since the Assembly of the Serb People was founded, told the Srna agency that Republika Srpska's future will be decided by its own institutions, not Sarajevo or foreign embassies [2]. No Republika Srpska government response to Lagumdžija was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on what both men said, which Oslobođenje and Srpska365 quote directly; the secession assessment is Lagumdžija's view.

items.title: Serbia Faces a Tight Sunday Vote as Student List Challenges Vučić
items.lede: Campaigning is banned until polls close at 20:00 on 25 October, and the BBC says analysts expect an extremely close result with few reliable polls.

sections.text: Serbia's election silence has been in force since midnight on 22–23 October and bans promoting candidates, calls to vote, and publishing result estimates until polls close at 20:00 on 25 October, with fines up to RSD 600,000 [3] [4]. Serbia's 6,450,523 voters choose among 18 lists for 250 seats at 8,392 polling stations [3] [5]. About 150,000 people rallied for the Student List around Slavija Square in Belgrade on 22 October, AFP reported via the Guardian [6]. In a preview published overnight, the BBC said reliable polls are scarce but analysts expect an extremely tight vote between Aleksandar Vučić's SNS and the Student List, with cardiologist Ilija Srdanović one of its leading figures [7]. Vučić calls the movement foreign-backed; the SNS gave the BBC no response [7]. Civil society groups report intimidation and misuse of public resources [6], and CRTA warned of threats and violence [8].

Confidence is high on the silence rules, voter figures, and rally, which the Guardian, BBC, BTA, RTS, and Telegraf report consistently; the closeness of the race is analysts' judgment relayed by the BBC.

items.title: Albanian Health Workers Join Student Protests and Demand Rama's Resignation
items.lede: Friday night outside the prime minister's office in Tirana passed without incident, as organisers called a national rally for Saturday with diaspora support.

sections.text: On 23 October, the 11th day of protests in Tirana, Albania, medical students in white uniforms joined students and lecturers outside the prime minister's office, and doctors, dentists, and pharmacists issued a statement calling on Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign for a transitional government [9]. Fewer than 100 young people stayed into the night, Periskopi reported [10]. On 22 October opposition MPs blocked parliament's podium with photographs of injured students after a debate was refused, Euronews reported [11]. Earlier, masked groups threw Molotov cocktails at police outside Rama's office on 21 October, and police answered with water cannon and tear gas [12] [13]. State Police reported 271 arrests over seven days [14][15]. The Health Ministry put injuries at 310, including 191 police officers, on 19 October [16], and official health data showed 320 injured, including 192 police officers, by 21 October [15]. Balkan Insight reported a video from 19 October showing police beating young people, one shouting that he is only 13; BIRN could not verify the ages [17]. No State Police response to the footage was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the 23 October protest and the quiet night, which RTSH and Periskopi report; confidence is moderate on the footage, which Balkan Insight could not fully verify.

items.title: Disabled Serbians Report Pressure to Back Ruling SNS Before Sunday Vote
items.lede: One woman says she was warned she might lose her care allowance, and an activist describes a widespread fear among people with disabilities.

sections.text: People with disabilities in Serbia face pressure to vote for the ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in the 25 October parliamentary election, Balkan Insight reported on 23 October [18]. A woman with a disability, speaking anonymously, said a representative of a major disability association, which depends on state or local funding, told her she 'might never receive the care allowance again' if she did not vote SNS [18]. A human rights activist described a 'collective fear', saying many vote for the ruling party even without direct threats, fearing loss of allowances they are legally entitled to [18]. No SNS or government response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because the account rests on anonymous sources in one BIRN report.

items.title: Kosovo President Sends Specialist Chambers Bill Back to Parliament
items.lede: The PDK, which sponsored the law curbing the Hague-based war crimes court, itself asked Justina Shiroka Pula to let lawmakers reconsider it.

sections.text: Kosovo President Justina Shiroka Pula returned the amended Kosovo Specialist Chambers (KSC) bill to parliament on 22 October for review at the request of the Democratic Party of Kosovo (PDK), less than three weeks after its approval, Balkan Insight reported [19]. The law aims to curtail the jurisdiction of the Hague-based court and followed weeks of protests by Kosovo Liberation Army veterans after four former KLA leaders were convicted [19]. The president's office said PDK asked that the assembly reconsider the provisions on the court's jurisdiction and mandate [19]. Her statement also reiterated opposition to any attempt to cast doubt on the liberation nature of the war [19].
Confidence is high, because Balkan Insight quotes the president's office statement; the statement itself was not read.

items.title: Georgia's Constitutional Court Rejects Every Opposition Motion in Party-Ban Case
items.lede: Judges rule on 26 October whether Georgian Dream founder Bidzina Ivanishvili must testify, as senior MEPs warn a ban would mean a one-party system.

sections.text: Georgia's Constitutional Court granted none of the 13 motions filed by opposition parties during three days of hearings on Georgian Dream's lawsuit to ban five opposition parties, Caucasian Knot reported on 23 October [1]. The plenum, chaired by Revaz Nadaraia, unanimously dismissed a request by former Prime Minister Giorgi Gakharia's For Georgia party to postpone proceedings until 13 November; SOVA counted 12 motions [2]. The court resumes on 26 October, when it will announce whether to question Georgian Dream figures, including Ivanishvili, as witnesses [1]. MEPs David McAllister, Nils Ušakovs, and Rasa Juknevičienė said banning established parties would be a decisive step towards a one-party system on the model of Russia and Belarus [3]. Council of Europe Congress co-rapporteurs called the case deeply alarming, warning thousands of citizens could be shut out of local democracy [4]. No court release was read.
Confidence is high that all motions failed, on the 26 October date, and on the European statements, which several outlets report; the motion count differs between sources.

items.title: Tbilisi Court Jails Georgian Journalist Dito Chubinidze on Treason Charges
items.lede: Prosecutors accuse the Asaval-Dasavali reporter of spreading disinformation since February, while his lawyer says he was simply gathering information for his reporting.

sections.text: Tbilisi City Court in Georgia ordered pretrial detention for Domenti (Dito) Chubinidze, a journalist for the newspaper Asaval-Dasavali, on 23 October, with Judge Eka Barbakadze fully granting the prosecution's motion, Interpressnews reported [5]. The General Prosecutor's Office charged him with high treason in the form of sabotage, alleging he has systematically spread false information and disinformation through media outlets and social platforms since February 2026 [5]. His lawyer Nona Pilauri said he categorically denies guilt and was acting as a journalist, and that he does not know former Prime Minister Irakli Garibashvili, whose published letter mentioned him [6]. No statement from Georgian press-freedom groups on the custody ruling was read by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because both accounts come from Interpressnews; the charges are prosecutors' allegations, and the evidence has not been made public.

items.title: Armenian Court Extends Ex-President Robert Kocharyan's Detention by Two Months
items.lede: The ruling came in his absence after he was hospitalised, the same day his son Sedrak's custody was also extended in the state-property case.

sections.text: Armenia's Anti-Corruption Court on 23 October extended the pretrial detention of former President Robert Kocharyan by two months, Hetq reported, saying the decision was issued in his absence after he was hospitalised with deteriorating health [7]. Earlier that day the court had extended the detention of his son Sedrak by two months, Armenpress and NEWS.am reported [8] [9]. Prosecutors argued Kocharyan could obstruct the investigation if freed; his lawyer Aram Orbelyan said the case materials do not justify custody and that the case has a political context, as Kocharyan leads the opposition Armenia bloc [10] [11]. He faces abuse-of-office, bribery, and money-laundering charges over state assets, including the Kaputak Sevan resort, allegedly transferred below market value [7]. Both deny wrongdoing [8]. Hetq names the judge as Sargis Dadoyan, while Caucasian Knot names Aram Grigoryan [7] [10].
Confidence is high on both extensions, which Hetq, Caucasian Knot, Armenpress, and NEWS.am report; the outlets conflict on the judge's name.

items.title: Russia's Grushko Calls South Caucasus an EU Arena for Confronting Moscow
items.lede: The deputy foreign minister says Brussels makes would-be members give up their independence by aligning with statements mostly aimed at Russia.

sections.text: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Grushko said the European Union treats the South Caucasus as an arena of confrontation with Russia, NEWS.am reported on 23 October, citing RIA Novosti [12]. Grushko said countries seeking EU membership or candidacy are pressured to give up their independence before joining, because the EU requires them to align with its common foreign and security policy statements, 80 percent of which concern Russia [12]. He did not name Armenia or Georgia in the remarks quoted [12]. No EU response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because the quote reaches L24 through NEWS.am citing Russian state agency RIA Novosti; the original was not read.

items.title: Georgian Ex-Deputy Minister Mikautadze Sees Ten-Year Term Cut to Three
items.lede: The plea deal follows his testimony against jailed former security chief Grigol Liluashvili and includes a GEL 1 million fine and asset seizures.

sections.text: Georgia's Prosecutor's Office said on 23 October that former First Deputy Economy Minister Romeo Mikautadze, sentenced to ten years for abuse of office and money laundering, had his term reduced to three years plus a two-year suspended sentence under a plea agreement approved by Tbilisi's Court of Appeals, Civil.ge reported [13]. He was fined GEL 1 million, barred from public office for three years, and will lose assets worth GEL 5.54 million, including an apartment in Madrid, Spain [13]. Prosecutors had said Mikautadze testified that he facilitated a bribe for former State Security Service chief Grigol Liluashvili, later jailed for 13 years [13].
Confidence is high, because Civil.ge quotes the Prosecutor's Office statement.

items.title: Armenian Anti-Graft Body Charges 24 over Vote Buying Before Stepanavan Poll
items.lede: Investigators say the bribes were meant to win votes for the opposition Strong Armenia party, whose mayoral candidate is now in pretrial detention.

sections.text: Armenia's Anti-Corruption Committee arrested ten more people on 23 October in a vote-buying case in the northern city of Stepanavan, bringing the number charged to 24, NEWS.am reported [14]. Those held face charges of giving, aiding, and receiving election bribes to secure votes for the opposition Strong Armenia party's candidate in Sunday's municipal election [14]. The Anti-Corruption Court placed Arsen Gevorgyan, Strong Armenia's mayoral candidate in Stepanavan, in pretrial detention for two months [14]. No Strong Armenia response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because one outlet relays the committee's account and the charges are untested.

items.title: Aliyev Hosts India's Jaishankar as New Delhi Backs Peace with Armenia
items.lede: The Indian minister came on Prime Minister Modi's instructions, and both sides stressed shared Global South positions on international issues.

sections.text: Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev received Indian External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar in Baku on 23 October, the presidential website said [15]. Jaishankar said he was visiting on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's instructions, and the two sides discussed political, trade, high-tech, and cultural cooperation and shared Global South positions [15]. Jaishankar said India welcomes the peace agreements Azerbaijan and Armenia reached in August last year and wants disputes settled through dialogue and diplomacy, NEWS.am reported [16].
Confidence is high on the meeting and the remarks, which the Azerbaijani presidency and NEWS.am report.

items.title: Poland Holds Second Georgian Suspect in Killing of Anti-Putin Cartoonist
items.lede: A court ordered three months' custody for the 22-year-old, accused of aiding the June shooting of artist Robert Kuzovkov near Belarus.

sections.text: Poland's Internal Security Agency (ABW) detained a 22-year-old Georgian citizen, named as Makhmud A, on suspicion of aiding and abetting the murder of Russian satirical artist Robert Kuzovkov, Polish special services coordinator Tomasz Siemoniak announced on 22 October, Civil.ge and OC Media reported [17] [18]. The National Prosecutor's Office said he was detained on 19 October in a car park on the A2 motorway [18]. Kuzovkov, known as Semyon Skrepetsky for cartoons mocking Vladimir Putin and Ramzan Kadyrov, was shot dead in Biała Podlaska on 15 June [17] [18]. He had reported death threats from Kadyrov supporters [18]. An earlier suspect held in June was using a Georgian passport [17].
Confidence is high, because two outlets report Siemoniak's statement consistently; the allegations are untested in court.

items.title: Two Georgians Held Since 2024 Near Tskhinvali Line Return Home
items.lede: Georgia's security service credits the EU monitors' hotline and raised the killing of Tamaz Ginturi at same-day incident talks in Ergneti.

sections.text: Georgia's State Security Service (SSSG) said on 22 October that two Georgian citizens detained on 16 September 2024 near Mejvriskhevi, by the occupation line of Russia-occupied Tskhinvali/South Ossetia, had been released and returned to Tbilisi-controlled territory, Civil.ge reported [19]. The SSSG said it used all instruments available, including the EU Monitoring Mission's hotline, and did not name the two [19]. The same day, the 135th Incident Prevention and Response Mechanism meeting in Ergneti, co-facilitated by the EUMM and the OSCE, discussed recent incidents [20]. The Georgian side demanded justice for the killing of Georgian citizen Tamaz Ginturi by Russian forces, condemned borderisation, and demanded the release of everyone still held [20].
Confidence is high on the release and the meeting, because Civil.ge relays SSSG statements; no de facto Tskhinvali account was read.

items.title: Russian Judge Named De Facto Premier of Georgia's Occupied South Ossetia
items.lede: Soslan Margiev chaired a court near Moscow until this year, and a native of Russia was named his first deputy days earlier.

sections.text: Marat Kambolov, declared winner of the September de facto 'presidential' vote in Georgia's Russia-occupied Tskhinvali/South Ossetia region, appointed Soslan Margiev de facto 'prime minister' on 22 October after the region's 'parliament' unanimously approved him, Civil.ge reported [21]. Margiev worked in Russia's judicial system for more than 20 years, including as chairman of the Lobnya City Court in the Moscow Region from 2022 to 2026 [21]. On 19 October Kambolov named Ekaterina Tolstikova, a native of Russia, first deputy 'chairman of the government' [21]. Emilia Gagieva was also reapproved as head of the region's election commission [21].
Confidence is high on the appointments, which Civil.ge reports from de facto decrees; no Georgian government reaction was read.

items.title: Söder Pushes Aigner for German President as CDU Claims the Pick
items.lede: The CDU leadership wants to name its own candidate for the January vote, reports say, setting up a test when Merz addresses the Bavarian party on Saturday.

sections.text: Bavarian Premier Markus Söder used his speech opening the CSU party congress in Munich on Friday evening to back Bavarian Landtag President Ilse Aigner as Germany's next federal president, saying 'that would be a great thing' while conceding the decision 'is made elsewhere' [1] [2]. He said he would repeat it on Saturday, when Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) addresses the congress [1]. The CDU leadership does not want to commit to Aigner and claims the right to name its own candidate, the FAZ reported citing party circles; Merz has not decided, and this is not yet a rejection of Aigner [3]. Söder also called for an 'extremist clause' to cut Berlin and Saxony-Anhalt out of the federal-state fiscal equalisation if the Left leads Berlin or the AfD takes power in Magdeburg, saying he would pursue it with Baden-Württemberg and Hesse [1]. He again rejected an AfD ban procedure, saying it would strengthen the party's martyr status [2] [1]. The federal assembly is due to elect Frank-Walter Steinmeier's successor at the end of January [3].

Confidence is high on Söder's statements, because ZDF and tagesschau quote the speech directly. Confidence is moderate on the CDU position, which rests on FAZ and Bild reports citing unnamed party circles, relayed by Deutschlandfunk.

items.title: Storm Luise Halts Trains in Karlsruhe and Injures Two at a Fair in Germany
items.lede: One person is in critical condition after a fair stand fell in Rhineland-Palatinate, and forecasters expect a second storm, Manja, to batter the North Sea coast Saturday.

sections.text: Storm Luise disrupted rail traffic in southwestern and western Germany on Friday, Deutschlandfunk reported [4]. At Karlsruhe main station, an object blown into the overhead line at platform 2 caused what travellers called 'massive sparking'; federal police switched off the power and no trains could enter for a good hour [5] [6]. Near Pforzheim a branch struck the windscreen of a regional train carrying hundreds of passengers, which stood on the line for about an hour; police reported no injuries in either incident [6]. Stuttgart's S-Bahn changed timetables on several lines after a tree fell on the track, and North Rhine-Westphalia saw several line closures [6] [4]. In Nastätten, Rhineland-Palatinate, a metal frame toppled at a town fair, seriously injuring two people, one of them critically [4]. A second low, Manja, is due on Saturday, hitting the North Sea coast and islands hardest [4]. No Deutsche Bahn statement on nationwide cancellations was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the Karlsruhe and Pforzheim incidents, because SWR and dpa cite federal police and police spokespeople. Confidence is moderate on the Nastätten injuries and the wider disruption, which rest on a short Deutschlandfunk summary.

items.title: Germany Cuts Its Strategic Oil Reserve to 82 Days to Free More Diesel
items.lede: The remaining 13.5 million barrels of Germany's G7 share will go mainly to diesel and heating oil, as Reiche also launched talks to shore up the country's 11 refineries.

sections.text: Germany is releasing further strategic oil stocks under a G7 decision, the Economy Ministry said, after an ordinance letting the stockholding agency cut its obligation from 90 to 82 days of supply took effect this week [7] [8]. Germany's share under the International Energy Agency key is 19.5 million of 100 million barrels; 6 million had been released by October, and the remaining 13.5 million will focus first on diesel and heating oil [7]. The IEA agreed the release in March in response to the Iran war, which drove up fuel prices [7]. Economy Minister Katherina Reiche (CDU) announced the step on the sidelines of talks launching a national refinery strategy, due for cabinet approval by the end of March [7] [9]. She warned that, under the EU methane regulation as it stands, 80 percent of German oil and gas imports would fail its requirements [9].
Confidence is high on the reserve cut and the barrel figures, because the ordinance text is published and Handelsblatt quotes the ministry. The methane figure is Reiche's own estimate.

items.title: Wadephul Says Istanbul Group Will Meet Regularly, Next Time in Germany
items.lede: The eight countries took no concrete decisions but agreed to work together to get Russian and Ukrainian grain out by new Black Sea routes, the minister said.

sections.text: Germany's Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul (CDU) met his counterparts from France, Britain, Italy, Turkey, Egypt, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia in Istanbul on Friday, the first meeting in this format, held at German and Turkish initiative [10] [11]. Afterwards he said it went 'better than we had dared to hope', that the eight agreed to meet regularly, and that the next meeting will be in Germany, though no concrete decisions were taken [12] [13]. He said the group agreed to work together so that both Russian and Ukrainian grain can be exported and new Black Sea sea routes found [13]. Wadephul said the eight were jointly sending a signal that they would not accept Iran and the Houthis 'blackmailing world trade', and urged Putin to end attacks on Black Sea grain shipments [11] [12]. The Foreign Office put Bab al-Mandab traffic at about 12 percent of world maritime trade [10]. No joint statement from the eight ministers was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the meeting and Wadephul's account of it, because ARD, Anadolu, Reuters, and the German Foreign Office report it. The agreement on regular meetings and grain routes rests on Wadephul's own statements; no outcome document was published.

items.title: Leaked Emails Challenge Weidel's Account of Illegal Swiss Donations to the AfD
items.lede: A July 2017 email bearing her sender ID says donations had been announced to her, contradicting her claim she learned of the 132,000 euros only weeks later.

sections.text: Leaked internal emails of Germany's far-right AfD suggest party leader Alice Weidel knew earlier than she has said about illegal campaign donations from Switzerland, Der Spiegel reported on Friday [14]. WDR and NDR found a July 2017 email bearing Weidel's sender ID telling two confidants that donations had been 'announced' to her to fund her social-media campaign and asking that the account be watched for incoming payments [15]. In 2017, 132,000 euros arrived in 18 instalments on her district association's account, nominally from a Swiss pharmaceutical firm; the payments were later ruled illegal, and the AfD paid a fine of almost 400,000 euros [15]. Weidel said at the time she learned of the money weeks after it arrived and was 'surprised' [15]. Prosecutors ended their investigation in 2021 without proof of collusion with the donor, and the emails come from an illegal hack [15]. Weidel's spokesman said she 'revises none of her statements', adding that she had expected neither concrete sums nor the Swiss payments [16].

Confidence is moderate on the email content, because it rests on media reporting of hacked material whose authenticity has not been publicly confirmed by the AfD. Confidence is high on the 2017 donation facts and the fine, which are long on record.

items.title: German Judge Orders Ukrainian Spy Suspect Held in Pretrial Custody
items.lede: Prosecutors allege the man gathered data on tank, ammunition, and explosives output and on NATO eastern-flank sites for Russian intelligence since at least July 2025.

sections.text: An investigating judge at Germany's Federal Court of Justice on Friday put into effect the arrest warrant against Ukrainian national Vadym Y., so he stays in pretrial detention, the Federal Prosecutor said [17] [18]. Federal police (BKA) had arrested him in the Oder-Spree district of Brandenburg on Thursday [19] [20]. Prosecutors say he was in contact with a Russian intelligence service through an intermediary since at least July 2025 and gathered information on production of armoured vehicles, ammunition, and explosives, and on personnel and military sites securing NATO's eastern flank [19]. Some of it was public; for the rest he allegedly pumped contacts in the European defence industry [19]. The case began with a tip from the domestic intelligence service [19]. Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Russian intelligence activity in Germany remains 'unchanged high' [18]. The prosecutor gave no further detail on the eastern-flank allegations, and no comment from Kyiv or Moscow was found by the cutoff [18].

Confidence is high on the arrest, the detention order, and the allegations as stated, because they come from the prosecutor's own statements and are reported by the Stuttgarter Zeitung and Al Jazeera. The allegations are unproven and no charge has been filed.
